stem:
Tara scores $14$ marks out of $25$ on a quiz. She wants this result as a percentage.

Which claim correctly converts the fraction to a percentage?

options.text: Scale only the numerator $14$ toward $100$ and leave the denominator $25$ unchanged.
Treat the part-to-part comparison $14:25$ itself as already a percentage.
Read the percentage as $25\%$, taking the printed denominator alone.

teacher.key_rationale: 14/25 scales by 4 to 56/100, so 56%. Scaling only the numerator, treating 14:25 as a ready percent, or naming 25 alone miss the fraction-to-percent step.
